name: Randy Feenstra

accounts.evidence: The official House site links to x.com/repfeenstra and twitter.com/repfeenstra.

notes: The official site still links the same handle that was on file (RepFeenstra, written in lowercase on the site), even though the hint says it did not work. I found no renamed handle. The failure may be a lookup problem rather than a rename; worth re-checking. Feenstra ran for Iowa governor in 2026; his campaign site feenstraforgovernor.com returned HTTP 522 both times, so no campaign handle was confirmed.

name: Mark B. Messmer

name: Mike Johnson

accounts.evidence: The official House site links to twitter.com/SpeakerJohnson.
The campaign site, paid for by Mike Johnson for Louisiana, links to x.com/MikeJohnson.

notes: The on-file RepMikeJohnson handle seems to have been replaced by SpeakerJohnson on the official site. SpeakerJohnson is tied to the office of Speaker; if he stops being Speaker, this handle may change again.

The Katherine Clark for Congress campaign site links to twitter.com/TeamKClark.

name: Tom Emmer

accounts.evidence: The official House site links to x.com/GOPMajorityWhip and twitter.com/GOPMajorityWhip, labelled as Congressman Tom Emmer's posts.
The Emmer for Congress campaign site (tomemmer.com redirects to it) links to twitter.com/tomemmer.

notes: GOPMajorityWhip is a leadership-office account; it would likely pass to a successor if the whip role changes. The on-file RepTomEmmer was not linked anywhere I opened.
